title: Each instalment is its own purchase
objectives: Explain why a years-old SIP can still carry an exit load.
Describe FIFO and how it decides the exit load and tax on a redemption.
body_md:
Every SIP instalment has its own purchase date. So exit loads and capital-gains tax are worked out instalment by instalment, usually first-in, first-out: the oldest units are treated as redeemed first.

## Why an old SIP can still have an exit load

A SIP that started six years ago still bought units last month. If the scheme charges 1% on redemptions within a year, those newest units carry the load even though the SIP itself is old.

## What that means in practice

- Check the scheme's exit-load terms before any switch, STP or redemption.
- Work out which instalments fall inside the load period, not just the age of the SIP.
- Tax is worked out per instalment too, so a single redemption can carry both short-term and long-term gains.
- Refer every tax question to the client's CA. We explain, we do not advise.

## The line to use with clients

Each instalment is a separate purchase with its own clock. That is why "my SIP is five years old" does not mean "no exit load".
example: A client wants to switch a six-year-old SIP in March. The oldest units are outside the exit-load period, but the last eleven instalments are not — so the switch is planned in two steps rather than one.
say: Each SIP instalment is a separate purchase with its own exit-load and tax clock.
Units are redeemed oldest first, so the recent instalments carry the load.
never: Your SIP is five years old, so no exit load applies.
Redemptions from a SIP are tax-free.

talk_track.title: Four facts every team member must know
talk_track.text: Four facts every team member must know. First, missed instalments have consequences: a monthly SIP is cancelled after three consecutive failed debits, and a quarterly or less frequent SIP after two. That's been in force since April 2024. Second, cancellation is quick: since the first of December 2024, cancellation requests must be processed within two working days, down from ten. Third, pause, don't stop: many fund houses and platforms allow a SIP to be paused for a few months; terms vary, so check them. Fourth, each instalment is its own buy: exit load and tax are worked out per instalment, oldest first.

check.q: On a redemption, which units are treated as sold first?
check.why: FIFO means first in, first out: the oldest units are redeemed first, so each instalment's own purchase date decides its exit load and tax.

check.q: Which of these is a redemption that may be taxed?
o: Every STP transfer and SWP withdrawal
check.why: Every switch, STP transfer and SWP withdrawal is a redemption, so gains on it may be taxed. Refer the client to a CA.

check.q: Why can an exit load apply to a six-year-old SIP?
o: Exit loads rise with the age of the SIP
Recent instalments may still be inside the exit-load period
SIPs always carry an exit load
It cannot; the load ends after three years
check.why: Every instalment has its own date, so the newest ones can still be inside the load period.
